blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content: The modern theory of resurgence began with the voluminous works of Écalle in 1981 [@e1; @e2] and 1985 [@e3]. This theory now plays a vital rôle in a remarkable number of diverse areas, to name just a few examples: nonlinear systems of ODEs and difference equations [@costin1; @kamimoto], algebraic combinatorics [@cfmt1; @cfmt2], enumerative combinatorics and quantum field theory [@BD; @MY], period integrals and string theory scattering amplitudes [@dk], wall-crossing phenomena [@ks] and matrix models [@mm]. blocks.content:
arXiv:2304.07001v3  [math.NT]  10 Apr 2025
RESURGENCE, HABIRO ELEMENTS AND STRANGE IDENTITIES
SAMUEL CREW, VERONICA FANTINI, ANKUSH GOSWAMI, ROBERT OSBURN,
AND CAMPBELL WHEELER
Abstract. We prove resurgence properties for the Borel transform of a formal power series
associated to elements in the Habiro ring that come from radial limits of partial theta series via
strange identities. As an application, we prove a conjecture in quantum topology due to Costin
and Garoufalidis for two families of torus knots.
